boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: A documented set of SDSU’s Hobo Day traditions and signature homecoming rituals.

cards.title: Hobo Day
cards.subtitle: SDSU homecoming celebration
cards.notes: Follow the official Hobo Day schedule during homecoming week, then watch the parade and football-game traditions unfold on Saturday.
cards.short_summary: SDSU’s long-running, hobo-themed homecoming celebration began in 1912.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies Hobo Day as its homecoming celebration and dates the first event to Nov. 2, 1912.
cards.access_notes: Event timing and locations vary annually; consult SDSU’s current Hobo Day schedule.

cards.title: Spot the 1912 Bummobile
cards.subtitle: Hobo Day parade icon
cards.notes: Look for the 1912 Model T Ford in the Hobo Day Parade; outside the festivities, find it displayed in the Union’s Hobo Day Gallery.
cards.short_summary: A 1912 Model T has been an integral Hobo Day element since its 1939 parade appearance.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that the Bummobile is a 1912 Model T Ford, first appeared in the 1939 Hobo Day Parade and remains integral to Hobo Day.
cards.access_notes: The vehicle appears in Hobo Day activities; SDSU says it is displayed in the Hobo Day Gallery in the University Student Union when not in use.

cards.title: Meet Weary Wil
cards.subtitle: Secret Hobo Day character
cards.notes: Watch Hobo Week programming and the football-game halftime reveal for the alumni character whose identity is deliberately kept secret.
cards.short_summary: Weary Wil is a central Hobo Day character whose identity is revealed at halftime.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says Weary Wil has been used as a moniker since 1950 and that the character’s identity remains secret until football-game halftime.
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of Hobo Day; consult the current Hobo Day schedule for event details.

cards.title: Meet Dirty Lil
cards.subtitle: Secret Hobo Day character
cards.notes: Keep an eye on Hobo Week events and halftime on Hobo Day, when this alumni character’s identity is revealed alongside Weary Wil.
cards.short_summary: Dirty Lil joined SDSU’s Hobo Day tradition in 1976.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that Dirty Lil first appeared at Hobo Day in 1976 and that her identity remains secret until halftime of the football game.
cards.access_notes: Presented as part of Hobo Day; consult the current Hobo Day schedule for event details.

cards.title: Bury the Razor for One Month
cards.subtitle: Hobo Week kickoff tradition
cards.notes: If you want to participate, attend the official kickoff and make your own choice about the month-long no-shaving pledge; no participation is required.
cards.short_summary: A Hobo Week ritual inviting participants to pledge not to shave for one month.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s 2026 Hobo Day schedule describes One Month Club as a long-running tradition where participants bury a razor and pledge not to shave for one month.
cards.access_notes: Listed by SDSU as a Hobo Week event; check the current schedule for date and location.

cards.title: Bum-A-Meal
cards.subtitle: Hobo Week community meal activity
cards.notes: Sign up through the Hobo Day program if it is offered, then meet the assigned host-home plans and participation details provided by organizers.
cards.short_summary: A Hobo Week activity pairing students with Brookings host homes for a meal.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s 2026 Hobo Day schedule says students may sign up to “bum a meal” from a host home in Brookings during Hobo Week.
cards.access_notes: Requires organizer-provided sign-up and host assignment; availability and details vary by year.

cards.title: Build for Bum-Over
cards.subtitle: Hobo Week cardboard-shanty activity
cards.notes: Bring permitted supplies and build a cardboard hobo shanty with others at the scheduled Bum-Over gathering in the University Student Union.
cards.short_summary: A Hobo Week build activity centered on cardboard hobo shanties.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s 2026 Hobo Day schedule describes Bum-Over as an event where participants build hobo shanties from cardboard.
cards.access_notes: Listed in SDSU’s Hobo Week schedule; confirm current time, room and permitted materials.

cards.title: Rally at the Rails
cards.subtitle: Downtown Brookings Hobo Week rally
cards.notes: Head downtown for the scheduled rally and use the official event listing to confirm activities, vendors, entertainment and any attendance details.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Hobo Week gathering with games, entertainment and vendors.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s 2026 Hobo Day schedule lists Rally at the Rails in Downtown Brookings with games, food trucks, entertainment and vendors.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled during Hobo Week; consult the official event listing for current details.

cards.title: Gather at BumFire
cards.subtitle: Hobo Week outdoor gathering
cards.notes: Attend only the organized event, follow on-site safety directions and check the current schedule for the location, weather plan and programming.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled Hobo Week gathering built around a supervised fire, music and games.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU’s 2026 Hobo Day schedule lists BumFire as a Hobo Week event with music, yard games and hobo spirit.
cards.access_notes: Attend only as an official programmed event; current schedule lists it near Sanford Jackrabbit Athletic Complex.

cards.title: Watch the Hobo Day Parade
cards.subtitle: Medary Avenue to Downtown Brookings
cards.notes: Choose a viewing spot along the official route, then watch student floats, the Bummobile and marching-band performances move toward downtown.
cards.short_summary: The annual homecoming parade is a signature public expression of SDSU’s Hobo Day tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the Hobo Day Parade begins on Medary Avenue and ends in Downtown Brookings, with student entries and marching-band performances.
cards.access_notes: Annual date and route logistics can change; use SDSU’s parade page for current information.
